# Writing a `data-model-entity` page

Generated from `data-model-entity`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Lives at** `product/entities/<module>/<kebab-name>.md` (module carried by path, not frontmatter)
- **Authorship** `curated` — an agent may draft it; a human approves
- **Freshness** stale after 180d
- **Template version** 1 — set `template-version: 1`

## Frontmatter

Required on this type beyond the base fields (`title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`):

- `instance-scope`

The template also scaffolds `template-version`, `common-fields`, `sources`, `related`, `confidence` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

`owner:` is fixed to `product` — do not change it.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{INSTANCE_SCOPE}}. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

The body also carries 5 placeholders written in angle brackets — `<LogicalType>`, `<entity>`, `<field_name>`, `<meaning>`, `<module>`. Each stands for content you write; replace every one, including in a row whose other cells you have already filled. Leaving one is an error (`unsubstituted-placeholder`).

## Where this type may link

This page lives in `product/` (layer 1).

You may link to `domain/` — and to other pages in `product/`.

You may not link to `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

## Sections

Keep every heading, in this order: `## Definition`, `## Data model`, `## Enumerations`, `## Invariants`, `## Lifecycle`, `## Relationships`.

**This type must not carry** `## Boundaries` — that content has another home.

**Table columns you may not drop:**

- `## Data model` — `Field` | `Type` | `Required` | `Searchable` | `References` | `Description` | `Example`

**Structured cells:** each takes the form its grammar defines in `wiki-cell-grammars.md` §Cell grammars and the grammar files it names. A value in any other form is an error (`cell-grammar`).

- `Data model › Field` — `field-name`
- `Data model › Type` — `logical-type`
- `Data model › Example` — `typed-example`

## What the audit checks on this page

Because of the declarations above: template-sections, section-order, table-columns, cell-grammar, template-excluded-sections. Every page is also checked for empty sections, heading restatement, callout types and code pointers. Run `/wiki-conformance-audit` to see the full list with its verdict.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
